newsitem.title: KENYA: Nairobi share index edges up, no market direction.
newsitem.headline: Nairobi share index edges up, no market direction.

text.p: The 20-share index edged up at the Nairobi Stock Exchange on Tuesday on stable prices but floor dealers said the market still lacked clear direction and it was not certain that gains of recent days could be sustained.
The index gained 1.74 points to 3091.59. Turnover was posted at 8.26 million shillings on 317,112 shares compared to 12.12 million shillings on 357,310 shares on Monday.
Deals totalled 281 compared to 298 on Monday.
"I would not be surprised if the index fell tomorrow. The point is that the market does not have a definite direction yet," one floor dealer told Reuters.

A broker said that there apeared to be a serious shortage of institutional buyers. These might have been lured away by high interest rates offered by commercial banks or by the Central Bank of Kenya (CBK) for government treasury bills.

"Look at the plantation sector. Most of these stocks have just announced good results but you cannot say that they have since seen magical price movements. You can simply say their prices are stable," the broker said.
He instanced Brooke Bond, unchanged at 176 on 1,389 shares, and George Williamson which gained just 50 cents to 66 on 4,076 shares.
In other plantations; Rea Vipingo Plantations opened 30 cents higher at 11.50 but fell back to 11 before adjusting to 11.20 on 10,250 shares. Sasini Tea & Coffee made a shilling to 52 on 500 shares.
Barclays Bank dealt at between 112 and 110 from 113 on 14,694 shares while Standard Chartered Bank dealt at between 46.25 and 45 from 47 on 2,950 shares.
Uchumi Supermarkets rose 25 cents to 40.25 on 2,620 shares, CMC Holdings dealt 550 shares at 61 and National Bank of Kenya 17.40 and 17.45 from 17.90.
